question: Febrile seizures by definition occur in children aged 6 months to 5 years.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Febrile seizures are defined as seizures occurring in association with fever (≥38°C) in children aged 6 months to 5 years (60 months), without evidence of CNS infection or other cause. A seizure with fever outside this age range requires a different diagnostic approach — below 6 months, always investigate for meningitis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The age range 6 months to 5 years (more precisely, 6 months to 60 months) is a defining criterion for febrile seizures. Below 6 months, seizures with fever must be investigated for meningitis/encephalitis rather than assumed to be 'febrile seizures.' Above 5 years, seizures with fever are less likely to be febrile seizures and require evaluation for epilepsy or other causes.
